steps.prompt: You know $4 + 6 = 10$. What do you think $14 + 6$ is? Why?

cards.title: A bond to 10 with an extra ten
cards.body: $13$ is $10$ and $3$. To make $20$ it needs another ten: the $3$ needs $7$ to make a ten, and the $10$ is already there. So $13 + 7 = 20$. Every bond to $20$ is a bond to $10$ with an extra ten on one side.

cards.title: Worked example: what goes with 16?
cards.problem: What number goes with $16$ to make $20$?

steps.text: Split $16$ into $10$ and $6$. Look only at the $6$.
$6 + 4 = 10$, so $16 + 4 = 20$. The answer is $4$, not $14$: the $10$ in $16$ is already one of the two tens.
Think of it as a missing bond: $12 + ? = 20$.
$12 + 8 = 20$, so $20 - 12 = 8$. Turning a take-away into a missing bond is often quicker than counting back.

cards.title: The common trap
cards.body: With $15 + ? = 20$, some people answer $15$ because $5 + 15 = 20$ looks right. Check: $15 + 15 = 30$. The missing number is $5$. Always ask: how many tens do I have, and how many do I need?

prompts: How does knowing $3 + 7 = 10$ help you with $13 + 7$ and with $20 - 13$?
